dominant_strengths: Serif headline 'Delete this workspace?' adds editorial gravitas, balancing the utilitarian destructive-action pattern with character.
Restrained red usage—icon chip, warning strip, primary button—creates a clear danger gradient without overwhelming the dark canvas.
Hierarchy is crisp: icon → title → body → warning callout → actions reads top-down with confident rhythm and spacing.
dominant_weaknesses: The composition is a textbook destructive-confirmation modal; nothing here pushes beyond Vercel/Linear conventions in structure or interaction.
Cancel button feels visually weak—thin border on near-black blends with backdrop, undermining the safe-default principle for destructive flows.
No friction mechanism (typed confirmation, hold-to-delete) for an irreversible action, which the copy itself emphasizes is permanent.
fix_priorities: Add a typed-name confirmation input to match the severity claimed by the warning copy.
Strengthen Cancel as the visual default (lighter fill or higher contrast) so muscle-memory clicks lean safe.
Differentiate the warning strip—maybe a subtle inner glow or icon shift—so it doesn't read as the same red as the CTA.
rationale.norman_balance: Strong visceral polish and solid behavioral clarity, but reflective trust suffers because the irreversible action lacks any real friction beyond a button click.
rationale.intent_fit: Yes—it's a competent, well-crafted destructive-confirmation modal, just not a distinctive reinterpretation of one.
